You are building MULTI-NODE MANAGEMENT UI + a node onboarding script for Nxeon, a VPS hosting platform (Next.js 15 + Prisma) at /opt/nxeon on Proxmox VE. Read /opt/nxeon/CLAUDE.md first. The platform is becoming multi-node: a `Node` model exists and the worker's provisioning is already node-aware via `pveFor()`. Your job is the admin UI to add/manage nodes and a bootstrap script that preps a fresh Proxmox host so a new server can be added and "everything works in synergy." Match the premium design system.

STRICT SCOPE — you may ONLY create/modify:
- /opt/nxeon/lib/actions-nodes.ts (new — admin node CRUD + health check)
- /opt/nxeon/app/admin/nodes/** (new — node list, add, detail)
- /opt/nxeon/app/admin/infrastructure/page.tsx (edit: link to node management + show per-node capacity)
- /opt/nxeon/components/admin/NodeForms.tsx (new)
- /opt/nxeon/scripts/onboard-node.sh (new — prep a fresh Proxmox node)
Do NOT touch: worker/, prisma/schema.prisma, lib/db.ts, lib/proxmox.ts, lib/actions.ts, other lib/actions-*, components/ui/, components/portal/, app/globals.css, layouts, other admin pages except infrastructure, config. Do NOT run build/git/systemctl. You MAY run `npx tsc --noEmit`.

SCHEMA (already migrated — do NOT change):
`Node { id, name unique, pveNode, apiUrl, tokenId, tokenSecret, publicIp, bridge default "vmbr1", subnetPrefix default "10.20.0.", ipStart 100, ipEnd 250, sshPortStart 20000, sshPortEnd 29999, natChain default "NXEON_FWD", storageNvme "vmdata", storageHdd "vmdata-hdd", capacityRamMB 56000, isPrimary, enabled, status NodeStatus(ONLINE|OFFLINE|MAINTENANCE), lastSeenAt, createdAt, servers Server[] }`
`Server { nodeId, node, plan{ramMB}, status }`
Import: `import { db } from "@/lib/db"`, `import { requireAdmin } from "@/lib/auth"`, and for health checks `import { pveFor } from "@/lib/proxmox"` (pveFor({apiUrl,pveNode,tokenId,tokenSecret}) returns a client with .get()/.node; call client.get(`/nodes/${client.node}/status`) to test).

BUILD:
1. **lib/actions-nodes.ts** (`"use server"`, all requireAdmin): 
   - `addNode(prev, formData)` — validate + create a Node (fields above; each new node MUST use non-overlapping IP/SSH-port ranges and a unique natChain vs existing nodes — validate against existing Node rows and return a clear error if ranges overlap; suggest defaults: node #2 → subnetPrefix "10.20.1.", natChain "NXEON_FWD_N2", ports 20000-29999 are per-node-host so can repeat since different hosts, but keep natChain unique).
   - `updateNode(prev, formData)`, `setNodeEnabled(id, enabled)`, `setNodeStatus(id, status)`, `testNode(id)` (calls pveFor(...).get node status, updates lastSeenAt + status ONLINE/OFFLINE, returns result), `deleteNode(id)` (refuse if it has servers or isPrimary).
   - Audit-log each mutation (db.auditLog.create).
2. **app/admin/nodes/page.tsx** — node roster: name, pveNode/host, status StatusDot, enabled, #servers, committed RAM vs capacityRamMB (MeterBar), primary badge, actions (test, enable/disable, edit, delete). "Add node" button.
3. **app/admin/nodes/new/page.tsx** + **app/admin/nodes/[id]/page.tsx** — add form and detail/edit (NodeForms.tsx client components using useActionState). Detail shows live status via testNode result, per-node capacity, and the servers on it.
4. **Edit app/admin/infrastructure/page.tsx** — add a "Compute nodes" section summarizing all nodes (link to /admin/nodes) and per-node capacity; keep existing content. (Read the file first; make minimal additive edits.)
5. **scripts/onboard-node.sh** — a well-commented bootstrap you run ON a fresh Proxmox VE host to make it a Nxeon compute node. It should (idempotently): create the NAT bridge (vmbrX with a given subnet, e.g. 10.20.N.1/24) + enable ip_forward + MASQUERADE, create the ZFS/dir storages matching storageNvme/storageHdd names, create the snippets dir + the nxeon vendor snippet, create the Proxmox API token (role with the same privileges as the primary — document the pveum commands), download+build the same cloud-init templates (VMIDs 9000-9004) OR document copying them, and print the exact values to enter in the Nxeon "Add node" form (apiUrl, tokenId, tokenSecret, pveNode, subnetPrefix, natChain, etc.). Take parameters via flags/env (node number, subnet, public IP). This is the "add a new server and everything works in synergy" piece — make it thorough and safe (never flush existing firewall, never touch running VMs).

No fake data. force-dynamic on pages. params/searchParams are Promises. tsc --noEmit must pass. Report: files created, and any assumptions about how a second physical node connects (same L2? separate? note that cross-node NAT/private networking between hosts is a documented limitation needing a VPN/overlay — mention it honestly).

1	# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform
2	
3	Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
8	- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
9	- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
10	- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
11	- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
12	- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).
13	
14	## Portals & design system
15	
16	- Customer portal (`app/dashboard/**`) and admin ops portal (`app/admin/**`) are separate sidebar apps sharing `components/portal/Shell.tsx` (sidebar, topbar, notifications bell, ⌘K command palette backed by `/api/search`).
17	- Design system lives in `app/globals.css` (glass cards, gradient buttons, navy palette) + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` + `components/ui/charts.tsx` (dependency-free SVG charts). Use these — do not add chart libraries.
18	- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
19	- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners).
20	
21	## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)
22	
23	- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id).
24	- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
25	- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.
26	
27	## Conventions
28	
29	- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
30	- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
31	- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
32	- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
33	- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
34	
35	## Commands
36	
37	- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
38	- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker`
39	- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
40	- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
41	- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`
42	
43	## Domains & TLS
44	
45	- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
46	- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
47	- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP.
48	- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.
49	
50	## Environments
51	
52	- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
53	- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080. Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
54	- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
55	- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at :8080 → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. The improvement agent should test changes on staging before promoting.
56	
57	## Safety rules
58	
59	- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
60	- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
61	- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
62	- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
63	- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
64	- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

1	#!/bin/bash
2	# Nxeon — build additional Proxmox cloud-init templates
3	# Mirrors exactly how templates 9000/9001 were built:
4	#   scsi0 on vmdata via import-from, ide2 cloudinit, vmbr1 net, agent enabled,
5	#   serial0 socket + vga serial0, cicustom vendor snippet, then `qm template`.
6	# Downloads cloud images to /var/lib/vz/template/cloudimg/ and registers each
7	# template in the OsTemplate table of both the nxeon and nxeon_staging DBs.
8	# Idempotent: skips builds where the VMID already exists; DB upserts on slug.
9	set -euo pipefail
10	
11	IMGDIR="/var/lib/vz/template/cloudimg"
12	STORAGE="vmdata"
13	VENDOR="backup:snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml"
14	DBS=(nxeon nxeon_staging)
15	
16	mkdir -p "$IMGDIR"
17	log() { echo "[$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z)] $*"; }
18	
19	# template spec: VMID | slug | display name | filename | url
20	TEMPLATES=(
21	  "9002|almalinux-9|AlmaLinux 9|AlmaLinux-9-GenericCloud-latest.x86_64.qcow2|https://repo.almalinux.org/almalinux/9/cloud/x86_64/images/AlmaLinux-9-GenericCloud-latest.x86_64.qcow2"
22	  "9003|rocky-9|Rocky Linux 9|Rocky-9-GenericCloud-Base.latest.x86_64.qcow2|https://download.rockylinux.org/pub/rocky/9/images/x86_64/Rocky-9-GenericCloud-Base.latest.x86_64.qcow2"
23	  "9004|ubuntu-22-04|Ubuntu 22.04 LTS|jammy-server-cloudimg-amd64.img|https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/jammy/current/jammy-server-cloudimg-amd64.img"
24	)
25	
26	register_db() {
27	    local slug="$1" name="$2" vmid="$3"
28	    for db in "${DBS[@]}"; do
29	        sudo -u postgres psql -d "$db" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c \
30	"INSERT INTO \"OsTemplate\" (id,slug,name,vmid,active)
31	 VALUES (md5(random()::text || clock_timestamp()::text), '${slug}', '${name}', ${vmid}, true)
32	 ON CONFLICT (slug) DO UPDATE SET vmid=excluded.vmid, name=excluded.name, active=true;" \
33	        && log "registered '${slug}' (vmid ${vmid}) in DB '${db}'"
34	    done
35	}
36	
37	build_one() {
38	    local vmid="$1" slug="$2" name="$3" fname="$4" url="$5"
39	    local img="${IMGDIR}/${fname}"
40	
41	    if qm status "$vmid" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
42	        log "VMID ${vmid} (${slug}) already exists — skipping build, re-registering DB"
43	        register_db "$slug" "$name" "$vmid"
44	        return 0
45	    fi
46	
47	    log "downloading ${name} image"
48	    if ! wget -q --show-progress -O "${img}.partial" "$url"; then
49	        log "ERROR: download failed for ${name} (${url}) — skipping"
50	        rm -f "${img}.partial"
51	        return 1
52	    fi
53	    mv "${img}.partial" "$img"
54	
55	    log "creating VM ${vmid} (${name})"
56	    qm create "$vmid" \
57	        --name "tpl-${slug}" \
58	        --memory 1024 \
59	        --cores 1 \
60	        --cpu host \
61	        --net0 "virtio,bridge=vmbr1" \
62	        --scsihw virtio-scsi-single \
63	        --ostype l26 \
64	        --agent enabled=1 \
65	        --serial0 socket \
66	        --vga serial0
67	
68	    log "importing disk to ${STORAGE}"
69	    qm set "$vmid" --scsi0 "${STORAGE}:0,import-from=${img},discard=on"
70	    qm set "$vmid" --ide2 "${STORAGE}:cloudinit,media=cdrom"
71	    qm set "$vmid" --boot order=scsi0
72	    qm set "$vmid" --cicustom "vendor=${VENDOR}"
73	
74	    log "converting VMID ${vmid} to template"
75	    qm template "$vmid"
76	
77	    register_db "$slug" "$name" "$vmid"
78	    log "template ${name} (VMID ${vmid}) built"
79	}
80	
81	rc=0
82	for spec in "${TEMPLATES[@]}"; do
83	    IFS='|' read -r vmid slug name fname url <<<"$spec"
84	    build_one "$vmid" "$slug" "$name" "$fname" "$url" || rc=1
85	done
86	exit "$rc"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# Nxeon — onboard a fresh Proxmox VE host as a compute node
# =============================================================================
# Run this ON the new Proxmox host (as root). It idempotently preps everything a
# Nxeon compute node needs, then prints the exact values to paste into the admin
# "Add node" form (/admin/nodes/new). Re-running is safe: every step checks
# current state before changing anything.
#
# What it does:
#   1. Create a NAT bridge vmbrX bound to a per-node /24 (e.g. 10.20.N.1/24)
#   2. Enable IPv4 forwarding + a MASQUERADE rule for that subnet (append-only)
#   3. Create the NVMe + HDD storages matching the Node's storageNvme/storageHdd
#   4. Create the cloud-init snippets dir + the nxeon vendor snippet
#   5. Create a Proxmox API role + user + token with the privileges the platform
#      needs (documented pveum commands)
#   6. Build (or document copying) the cloud-init templates VMID 9000-9004
#   7. Print the Add-node form values (apiUrl, tokenId, tokenSecret, pveNode,
#      subnetPrefix, natChain, sshPort range, storages, publicIp)
#
# SAFETY:
#   - Never flushes the firewall. It only APPENDS its own MASQUERADE/FORWARD
#     rules and only if an identical rule is not already present.
#   - Never touches running VMs. Template builds skip any VMID that exists.
#   - Never destroys storage. `pvesm add` is skipped when the storage id exists.
#
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CROSS-HOST NETWORKING — IMPORTANT LIMITATION (read before deploying node #2)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Each node NATs its OWN private /24 (10.20.N.0/24) behind its OWN public IP.
# This makes each node fully self-sufficient for provisioning, IP allocation and
# SSH DNAT — but it does NOT give VMs on different physical hosts a shared LAN.
#
#   * A VM on node-1 (10.20.0.x) CANNOT reach a VM on node-2 (10.20.1.x) over the
#     private network. They are separate NAT islands.
#   * The worker's iptables NAT chain (NXEON_FWD*) is rebuilt per-host from the
#     DB; it only manages forwards local to the host it runs on.
#
# If you need private east-west connectivity between VMs on different nodes you
# must lay an overlay/VPN over the public IPs — e.g. WireGuard mesh or a VXLAN
# fabric (Proxmox SDN "VXLAN zone") — and route the /24s across it. That is out
# of scope for this script; it is a deliberate, documented follow-up. For the
# common case (independent single-node VPS customers) per-node NAT islands are
# exactly what you want.
#
# Assumption: node #2 is a SEPARATE physical box with its own public IP, NOT a
# second NIC on the same L2 as node #1. If two nodes truly share L2 you would
# instead give them the SAME bridge/subnet and split the IP range — but this
# script assumes the separate-host model above.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

# ---------- Parameters (flags override env) ----------------------------------
NODE_NUM="${NODE_NUM:-2}"           # ordinal; drives subnet + nat chain defaults
SUBNET_OCTET=""                     # third octet of 10.20.X.0/24 (default: NODE_NUM-1)
PUBLIC_IP="${PUBLIC_IP:-}"          # this host's public IPv4 (auto-detected if empty)
BRIDGE=""                           # vmbrX (default: vmbr1)
NVME_STORAGE="${NVME_STORAGE:-vmdata}"
HDD_STORAGE="${HDD_STORAGE:-vmdata-hdd}"
NVME_ZPOOL="${NVME_ZPOOL:-}"        # existing ZFS pool for NVMe storage (optional)
HDD_DIR="${HDD_DIR:-/tank/backup}"  # dir-backed HDD storage path
SNIPPETS_STORAGE="${SNIPPETS_STORAGE:-$HDD_STORAGE}"
TOKEN_USER="${TOKEN_USER:-nxeon@pve}"
TOKEN_NAME="${TOKEN_NAME:-platform}"
TOKEN_ROLE="${TOKEN_ROLE:-NxeonProvision}"
BUILD_TEMPLATES="${BUILD_TEMPLATES:-0}"   # 1 = build 9000-9004 here; 0 = document copying
SSH_PORT_START="${SSH_PORT_START:-20000}"
SSH_PORT_END="${SSH_PORT_END:-29999}"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $0 [flags]
  --node-num N          Node ordinal (default 2). Sets defaults for subnet + nat chain.
  --subnet-octet N      Third octet of the /24 (default: node-num - 1, e.g. node 2 -> 1 -> 10.20.1.0/24).
  --public-ip IP        This host's public IPv4 (auto-detected if omitted).
  --bridge vmbrX        NAT bridge name (default vmbr1).
  --nvme-storage NAME   NVMe storage id (default vmdata).
  --hdd-storage NAME    HDD storage id (default vmdata-hdd).
  --nvme-zpool POOL     Existing ZFS pool to back the NVMe storage (zfspool). Optional.
  --hdd-dir PATH        Directory for the HDD (dir) storage (default /tank/backup).
  --build-templates     Build cloud-init templates 9000-9004 on this host.
  -h, --help            Show this help.

Environment variables mirror the flags (NODE_NUM, PUBLIC_IP, BRIDGE, ...).
EOF
}

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --node-num) NODE_NUM="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --subnet-octet) SUBNET_OCTET="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --public-ip) PUBLIC_IP="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --bridge) BRIDGE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --nvme-storage) NVME_STORAGE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --hdd-storage) HDD_STORAGE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --nvme-zpool) NVME_ZPOOL="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --hdd-dir) HDD_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --build-templates) BUILD_TEMPLATES=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "Unknown flag: $1" >&2; usage; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

# ---------- Derived values ---------------------------------------------------
[[ -z "$SUBNET_OCTET" ]] && SUBNET_OCTET="$((NODE_NUM - 1))"
[[ -z "$BRIDGE" ]] && BRIDGE="vmbr1"
SUBNET_PREFIX="10.20.${SUBNET_OCTET}."
SUBNET_CIDR="10.20.${SUBNET_OCTET}.0/24"
GATEWAY_IP="10.20.${SUBNET_OCTET}.1"
if [[ "$NODE_NUM" -le 1 ]]; then
  NAT_CHAIN="NXEON_FWD"
else
  NAT_CHAIN="NXEON_FWD_N${NODE_NUM}"
fi
PVE_NODE="$(hostname)"
[[ -z "$PUBLIC_IP" ]] && PUBLIC_IP="$(hostname -I 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')"

log()  { echo -e "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $*"; }
ok()   { echo -e "  \033[32m✓\033[0m $*"; }
warn() { echo -e "  \033[33m!\033[0m $*"; }

require_root() { [[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]] || { echo "Run as root on the Proxmox host." >&2; exit 1; }; }
require_cmd()  { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Missing required command: $1" >&2; exit 1; }; }

require_root
require_cmd pvesm
require_cmd pveum
require_cmd iptables

log "Onboarding node #${NODE_NUM} — ${PVE_NODE} (${PUBLIC_IP})"
log "  subnet ${SUBNET_CIDR} via ${BRIDGE} (gw ${GATEWAY_IP}), NAT chain ${NAT_CHAIN}"

# =============================================================================
# 1 + 2. NAT bridge + ip_forward + MASQUERADE
# =============================================================================
log "[1/7] NAT bridge ${BRIDGE} (${GATEWAY_IP}/24)"
if ip link show "$BRIDGE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  ok "bridge ${BRIDGE} already exists — leaving it as-is"
else
  # Append an isolated (no physical port) NAT bridge to /etc/network/interfaces.
  # We do NOT reload all interfaces (that could disrupt the host); we bring up
  # just this bridge with ifup.
  if ! grep -qE "^\s*auto\s+${BRIDGE}\b" /etc/network/interfaces 2>/dev/null; then
    cat >>/etc/network/interfaces <<EOF

# --- Nxeon node #${NODE_NUM} NAT bridge (added by onboard-node.sh) ---
auto ${BRIDGE}
iface ${BRIDGE} inet static
        address ${GATEWAY_IP}/24
        bridge-ports none
        bridge-stp off
        bridge-fd 0
        post-up   echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward
        post-up   iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s ${SUBNET_CIDR} ! -d ${SUBNET_CIDR} -j MASQUERADE
        post-down iptables -t nat -D POSTROUTING -s ${SUBNET_CIDR} ! -d ${SUBNET_CIDR} -j MASQUERADE
EOF
    ok "wrote ${BRIDGE} stanza to /etc/network/interfaces"
  fi
  ifup "$BRIDGE" 2>/dev/null || warn "ifup ${BRIDGE} failed — bring it up manually / on next reboot"
  ip link show "$BRIDGE" >/dev/null 2>&1 && ok "bridge ${BRIDGE} is up"
fi

log "[2/7] IPv4 forwarding + MASQUERADE (append-only, never flush)"
# Persist ip_forward.
if ! sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward 2>/dev/null | grep -q ' = 1'; then
  sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 >/dev/null
fi
if [[ ! -f /etc/sysctl.d/99-nxeon-ipforward.conf ]]; then
  echo "net.ipv4.ip_forward=1" >/etc/sysctl.d/99-nxeon-ipforward.conf
  ok "persisted ip_forward via /etc/sysctl.d/99-nxeon-ipforward.conf"
else
  ok "ip_forward already persisted"
fi
# Idempotent MASQUERADE (in case the bridge already existed without our post-up).
if iptables -t nat -C POSTROUTING -s "$SUBNET_CIDR" ! -d "$SUBNET_CIDR" -j MASQUERADE 2>/dev/null; then
  ok "MASQUERADE for ${SUBNET_CIDR} already present"
else
  iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s "$SUBNET_CIDR" ! -d "$SUBNET_CIDR" -j MASQUERADE
  ok "appended MASQUERADE for ${SUBNET_CIDR}"
fi
# The worker owns the NXEON_FWD* DNAT chain; we do NOT create/populate it here.
# We only make sure iptables is not blocking forwarded traffic wholesale.
warn "SSH DNAT chain ${NAT_CHAIN} is created + maintained by nxeon-worker from the DB — not by this script."

# =============================================================================
# 3. Storages (skip if the id already exists — never destroys data)
# =============================================================================
log "[3/7] Storages: ${NVME_STORAGE} (NVMe) + ${HDD_STORAGE} (HDD)"
if pvesm status -storage "$NVME_STORAGE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  ok "storage ${NVME_STORAGE} already exists"
elif [[ -n "$NVME_ZPOOL" ]]; then
  pvesm add zfspool "$NVME_STORAGE" --pool "$NVME_ZPOOL" --content images,rootdir --sparse 1
  ok "created zfspool storage ${NVME_STORAGE} on pool ${NVME_ZPOOL}"
else
  warn "storage ${NVME_STORAGE} missing and no --nvme-zpool given."
  warn "  Create it manually, e.g.:  pvesm add zfspool ${NVME_STORAGE} --pool rpool/data --content images,rootdir --sparse 1"
fi

if pvesm status -storage "$HDD_STORAGE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  ok "storage ${HDD_STORAGE} already exists"
else
  mkdir -p "$HDD_DIR"
  pvesm add dir "$HDD_STORAGE" --path "$HDD_DIR" --content backup,iso,vztmpl,snippets
  ok "created dir storage ${HDD_STORAGE} at ${HDD_DIR}"
fi
# Ensure the snippets content type is enabled on the storage that holds them.
if pvesm status -storage "$SNIPPETS_STORAGE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if ! pvesm status -content snippets -storage "$SNIPPETS_STORAGE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    warn "storage ${SNIPPETS_STORAGE} does not advertise 'snippets' content — enable it:"
    warn "  pvesm set ${SNIPPETS_STORAGE} --content backup,iso,vztmpl,snippets"
  fi
fi

# =============================================================================
# 4. Cloud-init snippets dir + nxeon vendor snippet
# =============================================================================
log "[4/7] Cloud-init vendor snippet"
SNIP_PATH="$(pvesm path "${SNIPPETS_STORAGE}:snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml" 2>/dev/null || echo "${HDD_DIR}/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml")"
SNIP_DIR="$(dirname "$SNIP_PATH")"
mkdir -p "$SNIP_DIR"
if [[ -f "$SNIP_PATH" ]]; then
  ok "vendor snippet already present at ${SNIP_PATH}"
else
  cat >"$SNIP_PATH" <<'EOF'
#cloud-config
package_update: true
packages:
  - qemu-guest-agent
ssh_pwauth: true
disable_root: false
write_files:
  - path: /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-nxeon.conf
    permissions: "0644"
    content: |
      PermitRootLogin yes
      PasswordAuthentication yes
runcmd:
  - systemctl enable --now qemu-guest-agent
  - systemctl restart ssh || systemctl restart sshd
EOF
  ok "wrote vendor snippet to ${SNIP_PATH}"
fi

# =============================================================================
# 5. Proxmox API role + user + token
# =============================================================================
log "[5/7] Proxmox API role/user/token (${TOKEN_USER}!${TOKEN_NAME})"
# Role privileges: everything the worker/web need to clone, configure, run and
# monitor VMs, allocate cloud-init, and read node/storage status. Mirrors the
# privileges of the primary node's platform token.
ROLE_PRIVS="VM.Allocate,VM.Clone,VM.Config.Disk,VM.Config.CPU,VM.Config.Memory,VM.Config.Network,VM.Config.Options,VM.Config.CDROM,VM.Config.Cloudinit,VM.Config.HWType,VM.PowerMgmt,VM.Monitor,VM.Audit,VM.Console,VM.Snapshot,VM.Snapshot.Rollback,Datastore.Allocate,Datastore.AllocateSpace,Datastore.AllocateTemplate,Datastore.Audit,Sys.Audit,Sys.Console,Sys.Modify,Pool.Allocate"

if pveum role list 2>/dev/null | grep -qw "$TOKEN_ROLE"; then
  ok "role ${TOKEN_ROLE} exists — updating privileges"
  pveum role modify "$TOKEN_ROLE" --privs "$ROLE_PRIVS"
else
  pveum role add "$TOKEN_ROLE" --privs "$ROLE_PRIVS"
  ok "created role ${TOKEN_ROLE}"
fi

# User (realm@pve). Create if missing.
if pveum user list 2>/dev/null | grep -qw "$TOKEN_USER"; then
  ok "user ${TOKEN_USER} exists"
else
  pveum user add "$TOKEN_USER"
  ok "created user ${TOKEN_USER}"
fi

# Grant the role at / (propagating). Idempotent — re-running is harmless.
pveum acl modify / --users "$TOKEN_USER" --roles "$TOKEN_ROLE" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
ok "granted ${TOKEN_ROLE} to ${TOKEN_USER} at / (propagate)"

# Token. If it already exists we cannot re-read the secret (Proxmox only shows it
# once at creation), so we leave it and tell the operator to reuse the stored one
# or delete+recreate.
TOKEN_SECRET=""
if pveum user token list "$TOKEN_USER" 2>/dev/null | grep -qw "$TOKEN_NAME"; then
  warn "token ${TOKEN_USER}!${TOKEN_NAME} already exists — its secret is only shown once."
  warn "  Reuse the secret you saved when it was created, OR rotate it:"
  warn "    pveum user token remove ${TOKEN_USER} ${TOKEN_NAME}"
  warn "    pveum user token add ${TOKEN_USER} ${TOKEN_NAME} --privsep 0"
else
  # --privsep 0 => token inherits the user's privileges (the role we granted).
  TOKEN_OUT="$(pveum user token add "$TOKEN_USER" "$TOKEN_NAME" --privsep 0 2>/dev/null || true)"
  TOKEN_SECRET="$(echo "$TOKEN_OUT" | grep -iE 'value|secret' | grep -oE '[0-9a-f-]{36}' | head -n1)"
  if [[ -n "$TOKEN_SECRET" ]]; then
    ok "created token ${TOKEN_USER}!${TOKEN_NAME}"
  else
    warn "token created but could not parse the secret from output — run manually:"
    warn "  pveum user token add ${TOKEN_USER} ${TOKEN_NAME} --privsep 0"
  fi
fi

# =============================================================================
# 6. Cloud-init templates 9000-9004
# =============================================================================
log "[6/7] Cloud-init templates (VMID 9000-9004)"
NEED_TEMPLATES=()
for vmid in 9000 9001 9002 9003 9004; do
  qm status "$vmid" >/dev/null 2>&1 || NEED_TEMPLATES+=("$vmid")
done
if [[ ${#NEED_TEMPLATES[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
  ok "all templates 9000-9004 already present"
elif [[ "$BUILD_TEMPLATES" == "1" ]]; then
  warn "missing templates: ${NEED_TEMPLATES[*]} — building via scripts/build-templates.sh"
  warn "  (9000/9001 are base OS templates; scripts/build-templates.sh builds 9002-9004.)"
  SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
  if [[ -x "${SCRIPT_DIR}/build-templates.sh" ]]; then
    STORAGE="$NVME_STORAGE" VENDOR="${SNIPPETS_STORAGE}:snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml" \
      bash "${SCRIPT_DIR}/build-templates.sh" || warn "build-templates.sh returned non-zero"
  else
    warn "build-templates.sh not found next to this script — copy templates instead (see below)."
  fi
else
  warn "missing templates: ${NEED_TEMPLATES[*]}"
  cat <<EOF
  Templates are NOT auto-built (pass --build-templates to build here). Recommended:
  copy them from the primary node so every node clones byte-identical images:

    # On the PRIMARY node, dump each template to the shared HDD/backup pool:
    for id in 9000 9001 9002 9003 9004; do vzdump \$id --dumpdir ${HDD_DIR} --mode stop; done
    # Copy the resulting vzdump-qemu-90XX*.vma.* files to this host, then:
    for f in ${HDD_DIR}/vzdump-qemu-90*.vma.*; do
      id=\$(echo "\$f" | grep -oE 'qemu-([0-9]+)' | grep -oE '[0-9]+')
      qmrestore "\$f" "\$id" --storage ${NVME_STORAGE}
      qm template "\$id"
    done

  Or run:  BUILD_TEMPLATES=1 $0 --node-num ${NODE_NUM}   to build them locally.
EOF
fi

# =============================================================================
# 7. Print the Add-node form values
# =============================================================================
log "[7/7] Done. Paste these into Nxeon → Admin → Compute nodes → Add node:"
API_URL="https://${PUBLIC_IP}:8006"
cat <<EOF

  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Nxeon "Add node" form values                                           │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  Node name        : node-${NODE_NUM}
  pveNode          : ${PVE_NODE}
  API URL          : ${API_URL}
  Public IP        : ${PUBLIC_IP}
  Token ID         : ${TOKEN_USER}!${TOKEN_NAME}
  Token secret     : ${TOKEN_SECRET:-<shown once at token creation — reuse your saved value>}
  Bridge           : ${BRIDGE}
  Subnet prefix    : ${SUBNET_PREFIX}
  IP start / end   : 100 / 250
  SSH port range   : ${SSH_PORT_START} / ${SSH_PORT_END}
  NAT chain        : ${NAT_CHAIN}
